clue.text: Enormous donation hard for English actor

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means one letter stands in the place of another, swapping in a new letter

parts.note: enormous means huge
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
E is the abbreviation for English; it is the letter swapped out
a grant is a donation of money

explanation.surface: A huge gift is made to an English film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X for Y' swaps letters: here the H for hard replaces the E for English at the end of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Grant is a well-known English film star, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: Leave house quietly to get sex

parts.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
'it' is an old slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone slips out of the house discreetly to find a sexual partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hop it' is British slang meaning go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase is a brusque order to go away, so it means depart or clear off.

clue.text: Persuaded old lecturer to cut notice period, to begin with, providing pass out

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word lands in its middle, splitting it open

parts.note: to get someone to do something is to persuade them
O is the standard abbreviation for old
to notice is to see

indicators.note: 'to begin with' tells us to take only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of period
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: An elderly academic was talked into shortening a notice period.
explanation.walkthrough: The lecturer's L slips in after the first letter of SEEP to make the familiar word for slumber.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall asleep is informally to drop off or lose consciousness, a gentle sense of passing out.

clue.text: Flautist forever ignoring son after golf

indicators.note: 'after' places the first piece of wordplay behind the second in the finished word

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word it belongs to

parts.note: forever means always
S is the abbreviation for son, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A flute player keeps going on and on, ignoring a son, after a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: ALWAYS loses its S and goes after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir James Galway is a famous Northern Irish flute virtuoso, so he is an example of a flautist.

clue.text: Great Greek agreed to be inspired by God

indicators.note: being inspired means being breathed in, so one word is taken inside another

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
views that chimed agreed with each other

explanation.surface: A celebrated Greek concurred because a god inspired him.
explanation.walkthrough: Bells that chime together sound in harmony, which is why chimed can mean agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was a renowned ancient mathematician and inventor from Syracuse, a classic example of a great Greek.

clue.text: Right-wing Republican entertained by dwarf

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's home

parts.note: toy describes a dwarf breed, as in a toy poodle
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A conservative American politician is being hosted by a very short person.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Conservative Party's members are called Tories, so the adjective describes conservative politics.

clue.text: Become very excited about eating a rice dish

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards
a word that is eating another holds it inside itself

parts.note: to flip is to lose control and get very worked up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets overexcited while tucking into a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: FLIP turned round is PILF, which then takes in A: PIL-A-F.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaf is a Middle Eastern and Asian dish of rice cooked in stock with spices.

clue.text: Mountain-climbing lead is willing to forgive

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: an Alp is a high mountain
an electrical lead is a cable

explanation.surface: A climbing rope's leader is ready to forgive a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: ALP read upwards gives PLA, then CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone placable can be calmed or appeased, the opposite of implacable, so is ready to pardon.

clue.text: Bachelor to leave remainder for Pierce

indicators.note: when something is told to leave, those letters depart and are removed from the word

parts.note: the balance is the remainder still owed or left
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A single man departs, leaving the rest to someone named Pierce.
explanation.walkthrough: BALANCE loses its opening BA. 'Pierce' looks like a name in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance something is to cut or puncture it with a sharp point, as a doctor does a boil.

clue.text: Lefty Whig spreads division

indicators.note: spreading letters out scatters them, so they land in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A left-leaning Whig politician sows division in the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' sounds political, but here it is a boxing weight class.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyweight is one of the boxing weight classes, which are known as divisions.

clue.text: Towards the end, priest turned over a new leaf?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that a petal is only loosely a kind of leaf

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: late means towards the end of a period
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: Late in life, a priest reformed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE plus P is turned over. 'Turned over a new leaf' reads as a fresh start, but the leaf is part of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a petal is a modified leaf, and petals open fresh when a flower blooms.

clue.text: Rebuild tiny crate? Sure thing

indicators.note: to rebuild is to take apart and put together differently, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to reconstruct a small box, answered with confident agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is something bound to happen, and 'a sure thing' is the idiom for that.

clue.text: Tesla worker assuming continent is part of Australia

parts.note: T is the SI symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetic flux density

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one word is taken into another

parts.note: Asia is a continent
to man a post is to work it; a man is a worker

explanation.surface: An employee of the electric car firm Tesla takes on a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' looks like the car company but is the scientific unit, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia lying south of the mainland.

clue.text: Part of plant found in repellent creme caramel

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the concealed letters are read backwards
letters found in a phrase sit inside it, running across its words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bit of plant has turned up in a dessert that someone finds disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with stalked flowers along a central stem, as in foxgloves.

clue.text: Grown-up arranged time to seize drug contaminant

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
to run an event is to organise or arrange it
T is the abbreviation for time
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An adult has set a time to confiscate a contaminated drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug sits between the first two pieces, so the whole of the rest seizes it, not just the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance added that makes something impure, which is what a contaminant does.

clue.text: Bishop rejected Bill's complaint

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: a bill is a fee charged

explanation.surface: A clergyman turned down someone named Bill's grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: B, then FEE read backwards. 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a grievance or gripe, as in 'what's your beef?'.

clue.text: Dart around to stop authority making rest area for frequent flyers?

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside a bottle's neck, so these letters plug the middle of another word
letters moved around are jumbled into a different order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
a bible is an authoritative reference work

explanation.surface: Moving a dart to block an official creates an airport lounge for regular travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters go inside BI-BLE. 'Frequent flyers' suggests airline passengers, but the flyers are garden birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird table is a raised platform in a garden where wild birds stop to feed, so a resting place for avian visitors.

clue.text: City girl in the mountains briefly exhausted racing across river

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Heidi is the girl of the Swiss Alps in Johanna Spyri's children's novel
the Elbe is a major river of Germany

indicators.note: something exhausted is emptied out, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of racing

explanation.surface: A town girl in the hills is worn out from running across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is the heroine of a Swiss children's classic; the river is German, fitting the German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidelberg is a historic German university city on the River Neckar.

clue.text: Development of rising affection, leading to marriage? Time for first bairn, at last

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, so the word runs backwards
'X for first Y' means one letter takes the place of the earliest occurrence of another

parts.note: affection is love
a marriage is a union
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: 'at last' points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of bairn, which T replaces where it first appears

explanation.surface: A romance blossoms into marriage, and then it is time for the first baby.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVE read upwards, then UNION with its first N changed to T. A bairn is a Scottish word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual change and growth over time, which is what development means.

clue.text: Landing zone's small step (each flap moves)

indicators.note: when letters move they shift position, ending up in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tiny step where something touches down, with flaps moving like an aircraft's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' suggests an aircraft, backed up by the flaps, but here it is the flat part of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfpace is a broad step or small platform between flights of stairs, a stair landing.

clue.text: Answer about angry husband ignored again and again

indicators.note: one word wrapped about another goes around it, holding it inside

parts.note: a reply is an answer

indicators.note: a letter that is ignored is dropped from the word it sits in

parts.note: heated means angry
H is the abbreviation for husband, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A furious husband is snubbed time after time when he tries to get an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion happens first; only what is left of the angry word goes inside the answer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly means happening many times over, which the phrase 'again and again' expresses.

clue.text: Nasty smell near vessel

parts.note: BO is body odour
at can mean near or by, as in 'at the door'

explanation.surface: An unpleasant odour lingers near a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a craft for travelling on water, so a boat is one.

clue.text: Gas, in French and Chinese and English

parts.note: et is the French word for and
the Han are the majority ethnic group in China
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone speaks idly in three languages: French, Chinese and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like chatter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless flammable hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas.

clue.text: Post Office blocking argument warning of crime?

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits within it, so one word lies inside another

parts.note: a tiff is a petty argument
PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

explanation.surface: Staff at a post office get in the way of a quarrel, maybe to warn of a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair because a tip-off need not be about a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is confidential advance information, often given to police about a planned offence.

clue.text: Staple food in bygone America

parts.note: bygone means past
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A basic foodstuff of America in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a basic dietary mainstay in Italy and much of the world.

clue.text: Spooner's solid fuel projection is possible energy saver

indicators.note: naming Reverend Spooner means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: peat is dried turf burned as solid fuel and a hump is a rounded projection; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A lump of solid fuel described as a way to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of PEAT HUMP gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat pump moves warmth from air or ground into a building efficiently, so may cut energy use.

clue.text: Sample advertisement showing petition

indicators.note: showing means put on display, so the letters are visible within the phrase

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A trial advert is displayed to support a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to make a formal request, which is what pleading for something does.

clue.text: Ring Christopher Robin's friend up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the name runs backwards

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear who is Christopher Robin's friend in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone a boy's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, so it is a ring shape.

clue.text: In Scotland, greet revolutionary about to abandon notorious lover, and dance

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: in Scots, to greet is to weep or cry

indicators.note: letters that abandon a word leave it, and are removed

parts.note: ca. (circa) means about, as with dates
Casanova was the infamous Venetian seducer

explanation.surface: A Scot welcomes a rebel who is about to desert a famous seducer, and then they dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' looks like a welcome, but in Scots it means to cry. CASANOVA drops CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and music style related to the samba.

clue.text: Tolerate Baron punching assistant

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so one letter goes inside a word

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
B is the abbreviation for baron

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with an aristocrat thumping his helper.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to bear or put up with it, usually in the negative.

clue.text: English Channel ebbs — get out of the way

indicators.note: a tide that ebbs flows back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Dave is a UK television channel

explanation.surface: The tide goes out in the English Channel, so boats should move aside.
explanation.walkthrough: E and DAVE together are read backwards. 'English Channel' looks like the sea between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or avoid something, stepping clear of its path.

clue.text: Decorated salesman's spiel reflected study

parts.note: patter is the fast persuasive talk of a salesman

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A salesman's pitch is considered, and he is honoured for it.
explanation.walkthrough: PATTER, then DEN read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patterned is ornamented with a repeated design, so it is decorated.
